div.head: Ger 4
div.ab: [4] Ac ic lære, þæt he do, swa ic ær cwæð: gyme ægðer ge ðæs selran ge þæs sæmran, þæt naðor ne misfare, gyf he wealdan mæge, ne corn ne sceaf, ne flæsc ne flotsmeru, ne cyse ne cyslyb, ne nan ðera ðinga ðe æfra to note mæge.

Ac ic lære þæt he do swa ic ær cwæð. gyme ægðer ge ðæs sel|ran. ge þæs sæmran . þæt naðor ne misfare gyf he wealdan mæge . ne corn . ne sceaf . ne flæsc . ne slotsmeru [could be as 17.]. ne cyse . ne cys|lyb. ne nan ðera ðinga ðe æfra to note mæge .

Ac ic lære þæt he do swa ic ær cwæð: gyme ægðer ge ðæs selran ge þæs sæmran þæt naðor ne misfare gyf heealdan mæge, ne corn ne sceaf, ne flæsc ne flotsmeru, ne w cyse ne cyslyb, ne nan ðera ðinga ðe æfra to note mæge.

Vielmehr rath' ich, dass er handle, wie ich zuvor gesagt habe: er achte sowohl des besseren wie des geringeren, damit weder missrathe, soweit er verfügen kann, Korn noch Garbe, weder Fleisch noch flüssig Fett [Schmalz oder Rahmbutter], weder Käse noch Lab, noch eines der Dinge, die je zu Nutzen [sein] mögen.

Rather I advise that he act as I said before: let him take care of both the better and the poorer, so that nothing goes wrong, as far as he can control it, neither corn nor sheaf, neither meat nor liquid fat [lard or cream-butter], neither cheese nor rennet, nor any of the things that may ever [be] of use.

But I advise that he do just as I said before: take care of both the better and of the worse so that nothing go wrong if he may prevent it; not corn nor sheaf, nor flesh nor morsel of fat, nor cheese nor rennet, nor any of those things which may ever be of note.

But I instruct him to do as I said earlier: care for both the better and the worse so that nothing will go astray if he can prevent it, neither grain nor sheaf, neither meat nor scrap of fat, neither cheese nor rennet, nor any of those things which might ever be of use.
div.note: B's ‘æfra’ stands so. Liebermann compares Gerefa 3 and Gerefa 13, 18.1.
rennet: Literally, “cheese medicine,” the enzymes used to curdle milk into cheese.
